title: Gen Z: Harnessing Your 20s for Early Wealth Creation
description: Starting your financial journey in your 20s offers a significant advantage due to the power of compounding and a longer investment horizon. Gen Z can leverage.

faq.q: Is there an ideal age to start investing?
faq.a: While any age is good to start, your 20s are often considered ideal due to the long investment horizon, allowing compounding to work its magic over decades.

faq.q: How much should I invest if I have student loan debt?
faq.a: Prioritise paying off high-interest debt first. Once that's managed, aim to invest a portion of your income while continuing to service any remaining lower-interest debt.

faq.q: What is an emergency fund, and why is it important for Gen Z?
faq.a: An emergency fund is a pool of readily accessible money (typically 3-6 months' worth of essential expenses) kept in a liquid account. It's crucial for Gen Z to avoid dipping into investments for unforeseen events like job loss or medical emergencies.

faq.q: How much risk should I take in my 20s?
faq.a: With a long investment horizon, Gen Z can generally afford to take on higher risk, meaning a larger allocation to equities, which historically offer higher returns over the long term.

faq.q: Should I consult a financial advisor in my 20s?
faq.a: Yes, a Certified Financial Planner can help you create a personalised financial plan, set realistic goals, and choose appropriate investment products tailored to your risk profile and aspirations.

faq.q: How can I avoid common investing mistakes like panic selling?
faq.a: Focus on long-term goals, understand that market fluctuations are normal, and avoid reacting impulsively to short-term news. Regular, disciplined investing through SIPs helps overcome emotional biases.

based_on.title: International Youth Day: Fewer responsibilities, longer time — how Gen Z can harness their 20s for wealth creation
